A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Native Hybrid Attention and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Retained material can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, LLM hybridization, efficiency, and ablation results in Tables 1–7 and the accompanying figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds an FDA study of inference-time architectural configurations in Table 5.

M1.justification: v3 introduces a limited extension involving randomized-window training followed by inference-time window reconfiguration for specialization (Figure 4; Sections 3.3 and 4.7.1). The underlying NHA recurrences, unified softmax, token shift, and chunkwise computation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained, including SlimPajama, recall and commonsense benchmarks, RULER, and broader Qwen3 evaluations. The new configuration study uses the existing FDA benchmark, and Table 9 uses previously evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix C.6 and Table 9 add Mamba-Llama-3 as a direct adaptation comparator. This differs from the Mamba-7B and Mamba2-H comparators already present in v1. Existing comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds a protocol evaluating one 24-layer NHA checkpoint under different full-attention ratios and placements, including pure-linear and full-attention configurations, without retraining (Table 5). Existing experiments retain their reported training budgets, context lengths, and evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.7.1 adds an FDA analysis of sensitivity to full-attention layer placement and ratio, extending the earlier component and window-size ablations. Existing memory/fusion, positional-encoding, slot/window, and memory-use analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 42 and representative single-run results, with the same statement that repeated training produced consistent performance. Neither adds run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. v3 adds FDA configuration accuracies in Table 5 and Mamba-Llama-3 results in Table 9. Table 9's NHA average of 70.82 reaggregates six existing task scores; Table 3's 70.31 also includes LAMBADA, so this is not an improvement in the retained model's performance.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), the chunkwise derivation, the MesaNet/Atlas discussion, and Appendix D's gradient-coupling analysis are retained. Architectural-duality discussion adds no new formal theorem, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and three introductory contribution statements retain the same substantive claims about unified hybrid attention, empirical performance, and pretrained Transformer hybridization. The added studies do not revise these main claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning the importance of layer placement, deployment specialization without retraining, and structural compatibility as an explanation for efficient adaptation relative to Mamba-Llama-3. Existing explanations of performance gaps and the limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 5 supplies the search model's layer count and block-size/index configurations; Table 9 specifies the new comparator's 12.5% hybrid ratio and 20B-token budget. Existing implementation details and code access remain unchanged. The randomized-window training schedule and search procedure are still sparsely documented.

R1.justification: v3 prunes and replaces supporting citations, adding works such as Big Bird, Retentive Network, GoldFinch, and The Mamba in the Llama. Appendix B replaces the MiniMax-01 example with GoldFinch, while Appendix C.6 adds adaptation positioning against Mamba. The overarching intra-/inter-layer hybrid distinction remains.

P1.justification: Localized passages and subsections are added for configuration search and the Mamba comparison, alongside small wording and author-footnote edits. The overall narrative, section order, and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the architectural-duality diagram in Figure 4 and Tables 5 and 9, lightly adjusts Figure 2, resizes appendix tables, and reflows existing displays. Retained empirical plots and memory heatmaps use identical image data.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, Table 5 provides useful direct evidence for inference-time configuration flexibility, and Table 9 adds a relevant adaptation comparator while preserving existing evidence. The gain is limited by sparse randomized-window/search details, unequal adaptation budgets, and the absence of a separately reported comparison supporting the new specialized-pretraining claim.
